Drawing on her experience as an educator and wellness scholar “to cultivate (培养) a hope practice,” Hanley-Dafoe roots her argument in the deep effect that a lack of hope – or hopelessness – can have on people, describing that state as like “being trapped in a room without doors or windows.”

Her perspective is not limited to the “internal battle” of the individual; she demonstrates the urgent role that hope plays in society, “offering us purpose when things fall apart.” Hope is tied, here, to resiliency (韧性), which is “about growing, learning, and unlearning how to show up” – all hopeful acts.
